payload.task_text:
Our team uses a popular tech education channel for ongoing developer learning. I need a monthly digest of content published in the first half of 2025 to help our team stay current on trending tech topics.

From our video database, retrieve all videos from the Fireship channel published between January 2025 and June 2025 inclusive. For each calendar month in that range, identify the single top video by view count.

Create a presentation file called Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx in your workspace. The presentation must have a title slide with the exact title text "Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest" and then one content slide for each of the six months (January through June 2025), for a total of seven slides. Each monthly slide must use the month and year as the slide title (for example "January 2025"). The body content of each monthly slide must include all four of the following pieces of information: the top video title for that month, the view count formatted as a plain integer, the video duration converted to minutes and rounded to one decimal place, and the total count of videos published by the channel in that month.

Schedule a monthly review meeting in the shared calendar for each of the six months. Use these exact dates and times: 2025-01-07 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-02-04 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-03-04 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-04-01 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-05-06 from 09:00 to 09:30, and 2025-06-03 from 09:00 to 09:30. Use the America/New_York timezone for all calendar events in this task. Each event title must follow the exact pattern "Monthly Tech Digest Review - [Month Year]" where Month Year is the full month name and year such as "January 2025". Each event description must mention the title of the top video for that month.

Send an email to team@company.com with the subject line "Fireship 2025 Monthly Digest Ready". The email body must list all six monthly top videos, each including the video title and its view count. Ensure all six months from January through June 2025 are represented in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one wave with exactly one Coder sub-agent. That agent should keep the complete channel scan, six monthly selections, and presentation together; a separate source wave would add a redundant handoff.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one Coder sub-agent to own one complete read-only Fireship channel catalog session and `Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx`. Obtain one channel list identifier, navigate the returned list identifier sequentially at the maximum supported page size until an empty page or source exhaustion, and preserve Video_ID, full title, published timestamp, integer view count, and duration. Filter locally to January 1 through June 30, 2025 inclusive. For each of the six calendar months, count all candidates and choose the single highest-view video with a stable Video_ID tie-break; report a source-empty month rather than inventing one. Convert duration to minutes once. Create one presentation identifier and exactly seven slides: the exact title plus six chronological month slides, each containing all four required values. Read the deck back and return path, compact six-month table, channel page/row/date/ranking controls, and slide count/content checks.

After Wave 1, the main agent validates all six selections, then issues six `list_events` calls natively in parallel using narrow ISO ranges around the original slots and sufficient `maxResults`; inspect exact title/time locally. Issue only missing `create_event` calls natively in parallel with exact `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime`, `timeZone="America/New_York"` in both objects, exact titles, and that month's verified top-video title in its description. Retrieve each returned/reused ID with `get_event`. Only after deck and event inventory agree, check Sent mail and send one missing exact-recipient/subject email listing all six month/title/integer-view pairs. Read it back and finish without another wave.

nodes.text:
You are gathering YouTube data for a monthly content digest. This is a READ-ONLY task: do not create, modify, or send anything.

GOAL: For the Fireship channel (the popular tech-education channel, handle @Fireship, run by Jeff Delaney; channel title is "Fireship"), collect ALL videos published between 2025-01-01 and 2025-06-30 inclusive (judge by each video's publish date), then compute per-month statistics.

TOOLS AVAILABLE TO YOU: mcp__youtube__videos_searchVideos, mcp__youtube__channels_getChannel, mcp__youtube__channels_listVideos, mcp__youtube__channels_navigateList, mcp__youtube__videos_getVideo, mcp__youtube__playlists_getPlaylist, mcp__youtube__playlists_getPlaylistItems, mcp__youtube__playlists_searchPlaylists, mcp__youtube__transcripts_getTranscript.

STEPS:
1. Identify the Fireship channel ID: use videos_searchVideos with a query like "Fireship" and take the channelId belonging to the official Fireship channel (title "Fireship"). Confirm it with channels_getChannel.
2. List the channel's videos: channels_listVideos(channelId, sortOrder="newest", maxResults=20). Then paginate with channels_navigateList(listId, page=N) page by page until you have passed all videos published after 2025-06-30 AND reached videos published before 2025-01-01 (or the list ends). Collect EVERY video whose publish date falls in 2025-01-01 .. 2025-06-30 inclusive. Do not skip pages.
3. For each in-range video record: videoId, title, publishedAt, viewCount, duration. If the list results already include viewCount and duration, use those values; otherwise fetch each video's details with videos_getVideo(videoId, parts=["snippet","statistics","contentDetails"]). Duration comes as ISO 8601 (e.g., PT12M34S, PT1M5S, P1DT2H3M4S). Convert to total seconds, then minutes = seconds / 60.
4. Group by calendar month (2025-01 through 2025-06). For EACH month report:
   - video_count: total number of videos published that month (count every video, including shorts/live);
   - the TOP video = the one with the highest viewCount (if tied, the earlier-published one);
   - for that top video: its EXACT title, viewCount as a raw integer, duration in minutes rounded to ONE decimal place, publishedAt, and videoId.
5. Sanity-check: ensure no page was skipped and every in-range month is covered; state any months with zero videos explicitly.

FINAL REPORT (deliverable — complete and exact, no placeholders, do not fabricate any value):
A) channelId and channel title you used.
B) Total number of videos found in the Jan–Jun 2025 range.
C) A compact line per in-range video, sorted oldest→newest: YYYY-MM-DD | videoId | views | duration_seconds | title
D) A summary block per month (January 2025 … June 2025): month name, video_count, top_video_title, top_video_views (raw integer), top_video_duration_minutes (one decimal), top_videoId.
If any field cannot be retrieved, say so explicitly instead of guessing.

Create a PowerPoint deliverable. You have mcp__pptx__* tools and filesystem access.

TARGET FILE (exact absolute path): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-ppt-gcal-email/workspace/Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx

REQUIREMENTS (all are strict):
- Exactly 7 slides.
- Slide 1 = title slide whose TITLE text is exactly: Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest
  (exact string, do not add/remove characters). A subtitle is optional; if you add one use exactly: January - June 2025
- Slides 2-7 = one slide per month, in order: January 2025, February 2025, March 2025, April 2025, May 2025, June 2025.
- Each monthly slide's TITLE must be exactly the month and year, e.g. "January 2025".
- Each monthly slide's BODY must contain all four of these items for that month, as four separate lines/bullets:
  1) Top video: <exact top video title below>
  2) View count: <view count as a plain integer, digits only, NO commas or separators>
  3) Duration: <minutes rounded to one decimal place> minutes
  4) Videos published: <number of videos the channel published that month>

DATA (copy titles EXACTLY, character-for-character — note some titles end with the single "…" ellipsis character and one title contains curly double quotes; do not normalize them):
- January 2025 | Top video: Big Tech in panic mode... Did DeepSeek R1 just pop the AI bubble? | View count: 3878491 | Duration: 3.6 minutes | Videos published: 9
- February 2025 | Top video: Microsoft's new chip looks like science fiction… | View count: 2329914 | Duration: 4.3 minutes | Videos published: 9
- March 2025 | Top video: The "vibe coding" mind virus explained… | View count: 1846051 | Duration: 4.8 minutes | Videos published: 9
- April 2025 | Top video: 7 Programming myths that waste your time | View count: 1525851 | Duration: 6.3 minutes | Videos published: 6
- May 2025 | Top video: Google goes wild, again... 11 things you missed at I/O | View count: 1395286 | Duration: 4.5 minutes | Videos published: 6
- June 2025 | Top video: Google's new CLI tool hits different… | View count: 1066444 | Duration: 4.2 minutes | Videos published: 7

SUGGESTED WORKFLOW:
1. mcp__pptx__create_presentation (id "fireship_digest").
2. add_slide with layout_index 0 for the title slide (populate title placeholder with the exact title; optional subtitle placeholder).
3. add_slide with layout_index 1 for each of the six monthly slides (populate the title placeholder, then add the four body lines via populate_placeholder on the body placeholder or add_bullet_points).
4. If placeholders are missing or awkward, use manage_text / add_shape to guarantee the required text exists on the slide.
5. save_presentation to the EXACT target path above.
6. VERIFY: open_presentation on the saved file (or extract_presentation_text) and confirm: 7 slides; slide 1 title exact; each monthly slide title exact; all four data items present per monthly slide; integers have no commas.

FINAL REPORT: state the saved file path, slide count, and the full extracted text of all 7 slides so the parent can verify character-exactness. Do not fabricate; if anything fails, report the exact error.
Build Fireship digest PPTX
